cards.text: This one's a song, a psalm of David, Israel's king, and he's talking straight to God with no warm-up. He opens with this: "My heart is steadfast, O God" and friend, he means it.

cards.question: David's heart is steadfast toward God. What does he say he'll do with all his being?

cards.text: Then David starts calling out, "Awake, O harp and lyre!" Friend, this man is giving a pep talk to his INSTRUMENTS.

cards.question: David is waking up his harp and lyre. True or false: next, David says he'll wait for the dawn to wake him up.

cards.text: Nope, David says, "I will awaken the dawn." Most of us are out here negotiating with the snooze button, and this man is waking up the MORNING.

cards.question: David's not keeping this song to himself. Where does he say he'll praise the LORD?

cards.text: Then David says why he's singing like this. It's all about God's loving devotion and His faithfulness, and how far they reach.

cards.question: How far does David say God's loving devotion reaches?

answers.text: To the edge of the sea

cards.question: True or false: David says God's faithfulness stops at the borders of Israel.

cards.text: Beyond the heavens, up to the clouds, and I spent YEARS thinking the lid of a junk drawer was the sky. Then David's praise turns into a prayer: "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens"

cards.question: David prays that God's glory will cover all the ___.

cards.text: Then the song turns a corner. Up to now it's been all praise, all harps, all sunrise.

cards.question: After all that praise, what does David ask God to do?

cards.text: David asks God to save with His right hand, so His beloved may be delivered. Hold on to your apron, friend, because next, God Himself speaks.
The psalm says God has spoken from His sanctuary, and His first words are "I will triumph!" No maybe, no we'll see, just I WILL.
Then God goes place by place: He'll parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth. Then He names Gilead and Manasseh.

cards.question: God says, "Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine" What is He saying about these places?

cards.text: Then He keeps going: "Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter."

cards.question: God calls Ephraim His helmet and Judah His scepter. What kind of picture is that?

cards.text: Then God gets to Moab and Edom: "Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal". I was in a junk drawer for years, and the only thing anybody ever tossed on me was a takeout menu.

cards.question: God has one more place to name: Philistia. What does He say He'll do over Philistia?

cards.text: Then David's voice comes back in, and now he's got questions.

cards.question: David asks who will bring him to the fortified city. Who will lead him where?

cards.text: Then David asks God two hard questions, back to back.

cards.question: What's the first hard question David asks God?

answers.text: Have You not heard our songs
Have You not seen our gifts

cards.question: True or false: in his second question, David asks whether God will no longer march out with their armies.

cards.text: Oof, that one's heavy, friend, and I asked something a lot like it from the back of a junk drawer for years. But David doesn't stop at the question.

cards.question: David asks God for aid against the enemy. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The help of man is worthless
His army is far too small

cards.question: David's last line: With ___ we will perform with valor, and He will ___ our enemies.

cards.text: And that's the last line of the song. It opens with a steadfast heart and ends with David counting on God for the win.

findings.problem: The true or false asks what David says next in the same line (wait for the dawn vs. awaken the dawn). The baker has to guess the wording of the second half of verse 2. Nothing they've seen lets them reason it out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup line "David's not keeping this song to himself" rules out the private wrong answer (the cave of Adullam) and the limiting one ("Only in Bethlehem"). The word "Only" also makes that wrong answer sound different from the others.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This card recaps verses 1 to 5 ("all praise, all harps, all sunrise") and tells nothing from verse 6, but it cites Psalm 108:6. It also says the song has been "all praise" up to now, which clashes with card 10, where the praise had already turned into a prayer at verse 5.
The citation doesn't match what the card uses. It cites Psalm 108:6 but draws only on verses 1 to 5.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The right answer "Respond and save us" is the BSB's first-person wording. The wrong answers are third-person paraphrases ("the land", "the people's sin"), so the right answer sounds more like the Bible and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question asks for the exact wording of David's question in verse 11 ("Have You not rejected us" vs. two other worded lines), which is guessing the words of a line. The setup also calls them "two hard questions", which rules out the mild wrong answers about songs and gifts.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup line "two hard questions" rules out the wrong answers "Have You not heard our songs" and "Have You not seen our gifts", since neither one is a hard question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he asked something like "Have You not rejected us, O God?" from the junk drawer for years. In his backstory he didn't know God in the drawer ("I don't know anybody important"). This adds something new to his backstory and contradicts it.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The last card recaps the whole psalm ("It opens with a steadfast heart and ends with...") instead of moving the passage forward. Verse 13 was already covered on card 15.
Stop 2's story cards are mostly plain narration (cards 2, 4, 8, 10 and 16). There's only one real joke (card 6), so the stop reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
